G2, the Chicago-based software insights platform, agreed today to acquire three prominent software review and discovery properties from Gartner: Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp. The deal brings four of the largest B2B review sites under a single roof and signals a shift toward unified, AI-driven software recommendation and buying experiences. According to the announcement, the combined business will include roughly six million verified customer reviews and tap into an audience of more than 200 million annual software buyers. G2 said it expects the transaction to close in the first quarter of 2026, subject to standard regulatory and closing conditions.
The market will watch closely for how the combined entity leverages its scale to influence search visibility and buyer influence metrics in 2026 and beyond.
Gartner, which currently owns Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp, has held these properties for years as part of its digital markets portfolio.

results.description: The acquisition brings together four of the top B2B software review destinations under the G2 umbrella, creating an unprecedented centralized hub for software buyers and sellers worldwide.
extra_snippets: G2 acquired Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp from Gartner in a significant B2B software review consolidation, creating a unified platform for buyers and vendors. Last updated on: Feb. 11, 2026 · Jersey City N.J., Feb. 10, 2026 · G2, the world’s largest software marketplace, has agreed to acquire three major software review and discovery platforms namely Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp from Gartner, Inc.

The deal was announced in late January and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2026, marking one of the most significant consolidations in the B2B software review ecosystem. The acquisition brings together four of the top B2B software review destinations under the G2 umbrella, creating an unprecedented centralized hub for software buyers and sellers worldwide. G2 will integrate Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp into its existing marketplace and data systems, building a unified platform with more than 6 million verified customer reviews and access to over 200 million annual software buyers.

The divestiture of Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp signals a shift in Gartner’s strategy toward its core research and advisory business, as it exits the software review and marketplace segment it once operated under Gartner Digital Markets.
